note: Larger than a typical feature — three sub-features (point, prioritise, edit) and 25 decisions. Consolidated into 8 units rather than 12 so each is still one commit-sized piece of work. Built sequentially by the main agent: subagents are not available in this session.
buildOrder: picking first, because Q-25 chose 'pointing feeling instant and exact' as what the effort goes into, and everything else stands on 'the part you got is the part you meant'. `integration` is last because a second agent is concurrently editing all four of its files.

units.what: pixel-exact picking — an id channel in the rasterizer, the part under a cursor, and the parts inside a drawn loop
units.note: raster.js changes are strictly additive — createFrame keeps its signature and drawTriangle's id argument is optional — so every existing raster test keeps passing unedited.

units.what: the protocol: what a pointed-at part, an annotation and a focus set look like on the wire and in a report
units.note: contracts/ is main-agent-only (Rule 5). Additive and defaulted throughout, so all sixteen modules that compile against it keep working untouched.

units.what: the browser's point, annotation and focus messages actually reaching the orchestrator instead of being discarded
units.note: A-011: images ride this socket, so serve() must raise max_size above the 1 MB default or a large crop closes the connection instead of erroring.

units.what: focus as standing orchestrator state — re-attached to every report until cleared, never drained like a note
move, rotate, scale, delete, duplicate, rename and set-material as real logged operations
units.note: Q-19 chose one shared history, which is why these are logged Operations rather than direct engine writes — replay, checkpoints and roll-back-N come for free.

units.what: the tool an agent calls to read what the operator pointed at, including the image — the one thing ActionReport cannot carry
units.note: ActionReport is a text dataclass; an image cannot ride it. So the report says an image is waiting and this tool returns it. Q-02 means the text half reuses describe_object's payload rather than inventing a second summary of the same object.

units.what: the browser half — selection and focus state, the canvas crop, the annotation composer's logic, and the gizmo/snapping arithmetic
units.note: Pure logic in its own files, the way camera.js was split out of scene-renderer.js — that split exists because a camera that could only turn left and right shipped from the one file with no unit tests.

units.what: the point-mode toggle, the annotation composer, the edit panel and the focus outline, wired into the real page
units.note: CONTENDED. A second agent is concurrently editing index.html, main.js, tokens.css and tests/index.js for its Connect UI. Built last, and reconciled against whatever is on disk at that moment rather than against what was read at trace time (Rule 5: check for uncommitted local changes before a phase starts).

units.what: an operator's own edit applying while the run is paused
units.note: Not in the original plan. Found while wiring the edit messages: perform() refuses while paused and Q-17 made pausing the precondition for editing, so without this the manual tools could never work at all.

removedUnits.why: Planned, then found to need no work at all: build_handlers registers every ops.OPS kind generically and build_registry collects SESSION_SPECS generically, so all seven operations and the new tool were picked up with no edit to either file. Verified at 40 kinds and inspect 9 -> 10, not assumed. Removed rather than marked green, because a unit with no test commit and no change is not a unit — its seams are declined with that evidence.
